posts.title: Almost There: Pre-Release
posts.description: The stable launch is almost here, and this pre-release build already has the latest features for you to start building with
posts.author: ov-studio
posts.html:
This is a pre-release (release candidate) build, not the stable launch build. The stable launch is coming soon, but this one is already packed with all the latest features, so you can start building today. Expect rough edges, and tell us what you find.

It brings the last big visual systems, a much sturdier network layer, and a result we're proud of: our Lua implementation is now faster than GDScript in all aspects.

See it live on the benchmarks page, and run it yourself.

Thank you

  • @ov-kivi — For actively contributing towards Vital.kit and Vital.sandbox.
  • @Rohatcengizhanbucak — For bringing security issues to our attention, which helped us get them all resolved!
  • @Ianec21 — For contributing and getting Vehicle Wheel functioning normally.

Updates

Security & Stability

  • Resources now run in isolated Lua environments.
  • Join rate limiting, and a version check when connecting.
  • Server event handlers are now local-only unless marked remote = true.
  • Safer asset downloads, stored per server.
  • Fixes for several crashes.

Gameplay

  • Virtual dimensions — Up to 65,535 isolated worlds, each with its own rendering, physics, and audio.
  • Vehicle wheels — Fixed, with a debug overlay for tuning.
  • Model sync — Component transforms and blendshapes now replicate to every player.
  • Audio signals — audio:start and audio:finish.
  • Mesh collision — Bodies no longer fall through single-sided floors and walls.
  • FPS limit — Servers can cap client FPS.

Players

  • Server logos — The window and taskbar icon switches to the server you join.
  • Nicknames — Set yours in the main menu.
  • Kick reasons — Shown in the main menu when a server kicks you.
  • Updates — Type update in the console to update to the latest version.

Visuals

  • GPU particles — Emitters with shapes, materials, mesh particles, and trails.
  • Trails — Ribbons that follow any node, such as a hand bone or a projectile.
  • Supersampled antialiasing — Render the 3D scene at up to 2x scale for smoother edges.
  • Shader priority — Control which shader wins when several cover the same surface.

posts.title: Road to Vital.sandbox
posts.description: Months of building, testing, breaking things, and building them better have brought us here
posts.author: ov-studio
posts.html:
We're taking inspiration from the freedom, creativity, and community that made MTA, FiveM, and Garry's Mod legendary—and pushing those ideas further.

Built from the ground up, Vital.sandbox is a true sandbox platform—not reverse-engineered, but purpose-built to give creators the tools and freedom to build their own worlds, experiences, and communities.

We're in the final stretch toward official release! All features planned for launch are implemented; we're now focused on fixing known issues, testing, and polishing everything for release. The remaining roadmap will roll out through future updates, bringing new features and improvements as the sandbox evolves.

Support us

Fuel the final stretch ☕

Help bring Vital.sandbox to launch!
Grab 50% off in our countdown sale and support the final push toward release.

Updates

Platform

Vault — Publish and maintain community resources right on the site. No manual forks or Git archaeology.

News — Project updates, delivered as they ship. Share any post with its own link preview.

Docs — API references, enums, signals, guides, and server configuration.

Roadmap — See the status of every system.

Benchmarks — Live Lua vs. GDScript results from deployed builds. Try them yourself.

Workspace — Manage servers, resources, applications, and staff reviews in one place.

Studio — Create logos, banners, and social assets.

Masterlist — Server heartbeats, logos, banners, and up to five genre tags. Tokens expire after 14 days of inactivity. Every submission is reviewed by our staff before it goes live.

Runtime

  • Console with structured logging and client/server commands.
  • Isolated Lua environments for each resource, with dependency resolution and start, stop, and restart controls.
  • Hash-verified asset streaming and concurrent client downloads.
  • In-game splash screen, plus an in-game main menu.
  • Windows builds are shipping; Linux is still on the list.

Core

  • Engine, display, screenshots, MySQL database support, and asynchronous queries.
  • Discord Rich Presence.
  • Models with GLB support, animation layers, blendshapes, and network synchronization.
  • Camera, webview, canvas, SVG, images, fonts, textures, and render targets.
  • GLSL shaders from files or source, including CanvasItem, Spatial, and post-processing shaders.

Graphics

  • Physical, panoramic, and procedural skies; SDFGI, SSAO, SSR, SSIL, glow, and volumetric fog.
  • FXAA, TAA, and MSAA, plus color grading.
  • Directional, point, spot, and area lights.
  • GPU particles with shapes, trails, materials, mesh particles, and signals.

Physics

  • Rigid, static, character, animatable, and vehicle bodies—with wheels.
  • Box, sphere, capsule, cylinder, world-boundary, separation-ray, and mesh collision shapes.
  • Raycasts, point and shape intersections, motion casts, and trigger areas.
  • Runtime collision generation and a physics debugger.
  • Up to 65,535 isolated virtual dimensions, with full replication. GTA-style world separation, without one giant shared-space traffic jam.

Misc

  • Audio: 2D and 3D sources, effect buses, and multi-format streaming.
  • Utilities: Math, strings, tables, timers, promises, threads, easing, files, HTTP, crypto, compression, events, input, keybinds, and performance monitors.
  • Networking: ENet transport with reliable RPC, ordered sync, auto-reconnect, and RTT.
  • Replication: Entity lifecycle, authority, late-join state dumps, and client interpolation. Physics, vehicle wheels, dimensions, animation layers, and reparenting sync too.

posts.title: Hello World
posts.description: A test post that doubles as a guide for writing new posts
posts.author: ov-studio
posts.html:
This is a test post. Copy this file to create a new one. It stays hidden until you add publish: true to the frontmatter.

Creating a post

  1. Create a new .mdx file inside content/, for example content/17-10-2026/my-first-post.mdx.
  2. The folder path and file name become the URL, so that file is served at /news/17-10-2026/my-first-post. Folders can be nested, and the same file name can be reused in different folders.
  3. Fill in the frontmatter below, set publish: true, and push to main.
  4. The Build News workflow rebuilds news.json and the site picks the post up within a few minutes, no frontend rebuild needed.

Frontmatter

Field Required Notes
title Yes Shown on the card and in the post.
date Yes YYYY-MM-DD. Newest posts are listed first.
description No One-line summary for the card and link previews.
author No Defaults to the repository owner.
tags No Example: [announcement, update].
cover No Image next to the post (cover.png) or a path from the repository root. PNG, JPG and GIF also work as the link-preview image.
publish Yes, to go live Anything other than true keeps the post hidden.

Writing

Posts are plain Markdown (tables and strikethrough work too). Raw HTML such as <br/> is fine. MDX imports and JSX components are not supported and are ignored. Images placed next to the post can be referenced by relative path, for example ![Screenshot](./screenshot.png).

Formatting

Regular Markdown works: bold, italic, links, lists and blockquotes.

Blockquotes look like this.

Use ## for sections. To give a group of items its own title inside a quote, start the quote with a ### heading:

Group title

  • First item
  • Second item

Code blocks are highlighted:

local function greet(name)
  print("Hello, " .. name)
end

greet("Vital")

Images

Put images in frontend/public/news/ and reference them by absolute path:

![Alt text](/news/my-image.png)
